label: EU(7)-PIM: spironolactone above 25 mg a day
title: Spironolactone above 25 mg a day in an older person
statement: Spironolactone at a dose above 25 mg a day is named in the EU(7)-PIM list as potentially inappropriate for older people. The reason given is a higher risk of high potassium and low sodium in the blood in older adults, especially at doses above 25 mg a day, so that regular checks are needed. The list advises a lower dose when kidney function is moderately reduced. For alternatives it says to consider other options that suit the reason for treatment. The published entry also gives dose notes by kidney function, which are not repeated here. This is the entrant's plain-words summary of the list entry, not the published wording.

plain_summary: Spironolactone at more than 25 mg a day raises the risk of high potassium and low sodium in older people, so regular blood tests are needed.

medicine_groups.name: Spironolactone
medicine_groups.note: Spironolactone tablets are 25 mg and 100 mg. Eplerenone (Inspra) is a different medicine and does not count. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: Review spironolactone when recorded age is at least 65 and the latest documented regimen totals more than 25 mg a day. Count only spironolactone taken by mouth. A cream or lotion applied to the skin gives no finding. For tablets, multiply mg per tablet by the number of tablets prescribed per day. For an oral liquid, multiply the labelled concentration in mg/mL by the total mL prescribed per day. Add doses from different strengths only when the directions say to take them together. A recorded age below 65 or a known daily total of 25 mg or less rules out the finding. Otherwise, if age or daily dose is unclear, report a possible finding and ask for the missing information.
cannot_be_seen: Why spironolactone was prescribed, for example heart failure, fluid from liver disease or high blood pressure. Also the patient's potassium, sodium and kidney function results and when they were last checked, whether the patient takes the dose on the label, and supplies from a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm the intended daily spironolactone dose or the patient’s age if either is unclear? If the patient is at least 65 and the current dose exceeds 25 mg a day, could you review the dose and the latest potassium, sodium and kidney function results?
